title: 7(a) Real Estate Appraisal Harmonization Act
official_summary:
7(a) Real Estate Appraisal Harmonization Act

(Sec. 2) This bill amends the Small Business Act to revise the loan amount above which a real estate appraisal is required for a commercial real property securing a small business loan. Specifically, the bill ties the amount to the federal banking regulator appraisal threshold. (Currently, an appraisal is required for a loan of more than $250,000.)

summary.headline: This law changes the loan amount above which a real estate appraisal is required for certain small business loans backed by commercial property.
summary.what_it_does: It amends the Small Business Act, which governs SBA 7(a) loans. Before this law, an appraisal was required for a loan over $250,000 secured by commercial real property. The law instead ties that cutoff to the appraisal threshold set by federal banking regulators. The summary does not state the new dollar amount.

who_it_affects.group: Small businesses borrowing SBA 7(a) loans secured by commercial real estate
who_it_affects.how: The point at which their loan needs a professional property appraisal now follows the federal banking regulators' threshold instead of the fixed $250,000 figure.
They must follow the new appraisal threshold when deciding whether a commercial property securing a loan needs an appraisal.
The number of SBA 7(a) loans that require an appraisal may change, which could affect the appraisal work they are hired to do.
